conflict_record.conflict: two active contracts assigned different meanings to a field both called 'pocket diameter'
conflict_record.resolution: NOT_A_VALUE_CONFLICT — A DATUM CONFLICT. The two numbers measure different things at different datums. Both are retained under explicit names and the ambiguous field name is retired.

entries.original_purpose: the PLAN-VIEW lattice module — the footprint reserved per pan so the 3x3 pitch can be resolved. It is a spacing reservation, never a cavity wall position at any elevation.
entries.derivation: 26.0 nominal pan + 2 x 0.30 manufacturing tolerance + 2 x 0.0 retention pocket add
entries.milestone_introduced: PALT-M1 / PALT-M2 (layout contract); the owner's M1 review explicitly corrected its class to CALCULATED_LAYOUT_HEURISTIC and NOT an industry or production standard
entries.note: pocket_module_mm(spec, PALT_P1_MECHANISM) returns exactly 26.6 only because ADHESIVE_FIXED retention adds 0.0. A retention strategy with a non-zero pocket add would move the module without moving any cavity wall — which is what proves the two quantities are independent.

entries.original_purpose: the moulded CAVITY diameter giving the metal pan radial seating clearance
entries.milestone_introduced: PALT-M4B (the module the owner declared INCOMPLETE)
entries.note: adopted as the A2 fit datum as an EXPLICIT DECISION, not inherited silently: it is the only one of the two that was ever defined as a cavity, and it is the value that lets a nominal pan seat. It still originates in an INCOMPLETE module, so it stays DESIGN_DEFAULT / NOT_MANUFACTURER_CONFIRMED.

entries.original_purpose: the visible mouth where the 0.6 mm rim fillet meets the flat deck
entries.derivation: sharp wall line at deck + 2 x rim fillet tangent offset
entries.note: a caliper on the top view reads this, not the fit datum. Reporting it as a discrepancy would be wrong — but the distinction has to be explicit and testable, which is what DATUMS provides.

retired_field.enforced_by: palette_recessed_tray_geometry.build_recessed_palette_tray raises RecessedTrayError when the key is present

unresolved: the 0.30 mm 'manufacturing tolerance' behind 26.6 is annotated 'pressed-powder pans have WIDE tolerance (R10)' — that is a POWDER/layout heuristic, not a drawn metal-pan shell tolerance. Using it as PAN_MAXIMUM_ENVELOPE is conservative and probably overstated. A real pan-shell tolerance is NOT_ESTABLISHED and needs a supplier drawing.

side_wall_draft_deg.basis: drawn pans are near-straight-walled; a non-zero value is available but unestablished

base_corner_radius_mm.basis: PAN_BASE_CORNER_RADIUS — selected in M4B-A2 by the flat-seating constraint, not assumed

floor_radius_mm.basis: inner floor-to-wall radius of the drawn cup

upper_wall_terminates_at.basis: the rim is a plain cut edge; no bead or curl is modelled

pan_layout_tolerance_mm.basis: the palt_p1 layout allowance — see the datum conflict record; it is NOT a verified shell tolerance

pan_shell_radial_tolerance_mm.basis: drawn metal pan shell, provisional; NOT the 0.30 mm palt_p1 layout allowance. A real shell tolerance needs a supplier drawing and is NOT_ESTABLISHED.

assembly_placement_radial_mm.basis: pick-and-place of the pan into an adhesive bed

adhesive_placement_radial_mm.basis: adhesive squeeze-out beside the pan base

thermal_dimensional_radial_mm.basis: differential expansion over a 40 K excursion: ABS at 9.0e-5/K on a 13.3 mm radius against a metal pan at 2.3e-5/K on 13.0 mm

tolerance_stack.note: RSS governs because the six contributors are independent and a worst-case stack on a decorative pocket would be unreasonably conservative. The worst-case figure is reported alongside so the owner can overrule.

fit_datum_decision.reason: 26.6 is a plan-view layout module; it was never a cavity dimension. M4B-A used it as one.

selection.rule: smallest tested base radius meeting every condition in the owner's decision rule
selection.decided_by: all tested radii [0.3, 0.4, 0.5] satisfy every condition, so the rule's own tie-break — the SMALLEST tested radius — selects 0.3 mm at 0.249767 mm governing clearance against a 0.162853 mm engineering minimum. A radius is needed at all because the sharp-cornered control reaches only 0.150142 mm, which is BELOW that minimum.
selection.why_a_radius_is_required: at the corrected fit datum a sharp-cornered pan does clear (0.150142 mm) and does seat flat, but by 0.012422 mm — so it establishes GEOMETRIC clearance and fails ENGINEERING clearance. The base radius buys margin, it does not rescue a collision.
selection.not_decided_by: mesh identity preservation, visual plausibility, or ease of implementation

strategies.description: keep the current pocket functional diameter and a sharp-cornered pan; cut the floor fillet to the calculated non-interference maximum

seating.note: a positive margin means the whole flat base is carried by the flat pocket floor; negative means the base overhangs onto the fillet and the pan is carried on a ring

ENGINEERING_CLEARANCE.criterion: governing clearance >= the RSS tolerance stack AND the pan seats on its flat base

layout_impact_3x3.note: no strategy moves the 3x3 pitch; the pan field and the 116 mm external envelope are untouched

max_material_pan_check.note: the 0.30 mm layout allowance taken literally as a pan shell tolerance; see the datum conflict record — it is a powder/layout heuristic, so this is a conservative bound, not a verified requirement

strategies.visual_implications: a smaller internal fillet is not visible from above, but it sharpens the pocket's internal corner

datum_error_demonstrated.conclusion: the M4B-A interference was a DATUM ERROR, not a physical conflict: the same sharp pan clears once the pocket is built at the fit datum instead of the layout module. It still does not reach the engineering minimum, which is what the pan base radius is for.

resolution_matrix.note: strategy B is evaluated at its own stated minimum (26.7084). At the corrected fit datum of 26.8 the pocket already exceeds that, so 'enlargement' is a no-op — see the controls.
